title: Interpreting and Controlling Model Behavior via Constitutions for Atomic Concept Edits
abstract: arXiv:2602.00092v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We introduce a black-box interpretability framework that learns a verifiable constitution: a natural language summary of how changes to a prompt affect a model's specific behavior, such as its alignment, correctness, or adherence to constraints. Our method leverages atomic concept edits (ACEs), which are targeted operations that add, remove, or replace an interpretable concept in the input prompt. By systematically applying ACEs and observing the resulting effects on model behavior across various tasks, our framework learns a causal mapping from edits to predictable outcomes. This learned constitution provides deep, generalizable insights into the model. Empirically, we validate our approach across diverse tasks, including mathematical reasoning and text-to-image alignment, for controlling and understanding model behavior. tldr: 该论文提出了一个黑盒可解释性框架，通过原子概念编辑（ACE）系统地学习一种可验证的自然语言“宪法”，建立提示词编辑与模型行为之间的因果映射，从而实现对模型行为的深入解释与有效控制。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a black-box interpretability framework that learns a verifiable natural language "constitution" through atomic concept edits (ACEs), establishing a causal mapping between prompt edits and model behavior to enable deep interpretation and effective control of models.
